clue.text: Election date endlessly changed providing diversion

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters gathered here are put into a new order
endlessly means the word date loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Moving the date of an election serves to distract voters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims DATE to DAT; 'changed' shuffles ELECTION plus DAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Delectation is enjoyment or entertainment, which is what a diversion provides.

clue.text: Saw wolf clothed in back of false sheep

indicators.note: clothed in says one piece is wrapped inside the letters of another
back of picks out the final letter of the word false

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
to wolf food is to pig it, eat greedily

explanation.surface: A wolf in sheep's clothing, the old fable, seen through a deceitful disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' is the noun meaning a saying, not the past tense of see.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or maxim, and an epigram is a pithy saying.

clue.text: Terribly stern with cane producing delights

indicators.note: Terribly signals the letters are to be scrambled into something else

explanation.surface: A severe teacher wielding the cane gives pupils anything but delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' rearranges STERN and CANE; 'delights' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to charm or enchant them, so it is to delight them.

clue.text: Check Middle Eastern currency in Iran

indicators.note: Middle takes the central letter of the seven-letter word Eastern

parts.note: the rial is the monetary unit of Iran

explanation.surface: Looking into the money of a Middle Eastern country such as Iran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle Eastern' looks like one phrase, but 'Middle' picks T from the centre of 'Eastern'.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial is a test or check of something's quality.

clue.text: Vehicle for Schwarzenegger, say, after 'Terminator' ends

indicators.note: after places the second piece behind the first in the answer
ends takes the first and last letters of the film title Terminator

parts.note: Arnold Schwarzenegger is an example of an actor

explanation.surface: A film-star car, perhaps, for Schwarzenegger once the Terminator movies finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vehicle' suggests a star vehicle film, but means a farm machine here.
explanation.definitionFit: A tractor is a motor vehicle used for pulling farm machinery.

clue.text: Horror if I celebrate, taking crack

indicators.note: taking says the answer is held within the run of words before it

explanation.surface: Someone horrified at celebrating while taking drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: An orifice is an opening, a hole or crack in something.

clue.text: One makes a noise from passing wind!

definitions.text: One makes a noise from passing wind!

parts.words: One makes a noise from passing wind!
parts.note: the lavatorial reading hides an instrument whose strings sound when a breeze blows across them

explanation.definitionFit: This stringed instrument is played by the wind, named after Aeolus, Greek keeper of winds.

clue.text: Country where runny Brie's before appetising starter

indicators.note: before puts the shuffled piece ahead of the next
runny signals the cheese name and its s are to be mixed up
starter picks the first letter of the word appetising

explanation.surface: A nation where ripe Brie comes ahead of an appetiser course.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as 'is' on the surface but supplies a letter to the cheese anagram here.
explanation.definitionFit: Serbia is a country in the Balkans in south-eastern Europe.

clue.text: Gray, for example, put in English syllabus

indicators.note: put in says one piece goes inside the others

parts.note: a syllabus is a list of topics

explanation.surface: The poet Gray is an example of someone on the English literature syllabus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for example' is not part of the definition: Gray alone is the definition, and 'for example' gives EG. Thomas Gray wrote the famous Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Gray is renowned for his Elegy, so he is a writer of elegies.

clue.text: Type tending to the right?

parts.note: sounds like a description of a political conservative but means printed lettering that slopes rightward

explanation.definitionFit: Italic typeface slants to the right, so it is a kind of type leaning that way.

clue.text: Size of certain guys covered in flesh

indicators.note: covered in says the pieces sit inside another word

parts.note: flesh is meat
certain means sure
guys are men

explanation.surface: How big some men are, judged by the flesh on them.
explanation.definitionFit: A measurement is a dimension or size of something.

clue.text: Republic lying initially next to Spain and Portugal

indicators.note: next to places the two pieces side by side
initially takes the opening letter of the word lying

parts.note: Iberia is the peninsula containing Spain and Portugal

explanation.surface: A country said to lie beside Spain and Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberia is a West African republic, founded by freed American slaves.

clue.text: Insects circling a taut, empty web

indicators.note: circling says one word goes round the following pieces

parts.note: lice are small insects

indicators.note: empty removes the inside of the word taut, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: Bugs going round a tightly strung spider's web.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice is a crisscross framework, like a web of interwoven strips.

clue.text: Member following a Labour leader creates dismay

indicators.note: following puts the member piece behind the others
leader picks the first letter of the word Labour

parts.note: an arm is a member, or limb, of the body

explanation.surface: An MP lining up behind the Labour leader causes consternation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests an MP; it is a limb. 'creates' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm is sudden fear or anxiety, much the same as dismay.

clue.text: Dismal end of White Queen left in game

indicators.note: in says the gathered letters go inside another word

parts.note: chess is a board game

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the word White

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for Queen

explanation.surface: A gloomy outcome when the white queen is left stranded in a game of chess.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture is apt: CHESS is the game, though White Queen is not one piece here.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerless means gloomy and joyless, which is what dismal describes.

clue.text: Goal, always say, to get try

indicators.note: say signals the words are spoken, giving a word that sounds like them

parts.note: an end is a goal or aim; ever means always

explanation.surface: Striving for a goal, always seeking to score a try.
explanation.walkthrough: The rugby picture of goals and tries misleads; 'try' means attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: To endeavour is to attempt or make an effort, the same as to try.

clue.text: After getting spliced, he's snared and controlled

indicators.note: spliced suggests the letters are cut and rejoined in a new order

explanation.surface: After marrying, a husband feels trapped and kept on a tight rein.
explanation.definitionFit: To harness is to bring under control, as with a horse in a harness.

clue.text: Pound or Auden poem

indicators.note: to pound is to beat, so the letters are battered into a new order

explanation.surface: A verse by either of two poets, Ezra Pound or W H Auden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like the poet Ezra Pound but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondeau is a French verse form with a refrain, a type of poem.

clue.text: One down in match? It's incontestable

indicators.note: in says the two letters go inside another word

parts.note: a match is a sporting event
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A player getting knocked down in a match beyond dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: Something evident is plain and obvious, hence beyond dispute.

clue.text: He plays pibroch first in support

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the next word

parts.note: a pier is a supporting pillar

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word pibroch

explanation.surface: A bagpipe player starting a pibroch in support of something.
explanation.walkthrough: A pibroch is a piece of classical Scottish bagpipe music.
explanation.definitionFit: A piper is one who plays the pipes, so he plays.

clue.text: Steals from sanctimonious judges

parts.note: pi is a short form of pious, meaning sanctimonious
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: Self-righteous judges taking things that are not theirs.
explanation.definitionFit: To pirate is to steal or copy without permission, so pirates means steals.

clue.text: Prospect, not finding gold, in canal

indicators.note: not finding says some letters are missing from the word

parts.note: a prospect is a wide view, a panorama
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A prospector failing to strike gold along a canal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prospect' suggests prospecting for gold, but means a view.
explanation.definitionFit: The Panama Canal links the Atlantic and Pacific oceans across Central America.

clue.text: Rook, a chessman taking knight for position

indicators.note: taking means one piece captures another within it

parts.note: R is the chess notation for rook
the king is a chessman
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: In chess, a rook and another piece capture a knight to gain position.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranking is a place or standing in an order, a position.

clue.text: He's finished with good single run

parts.note: one means single
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A batsman out after scoring a single run.
explanation.definitionFit: A goner is someone who is doomed or done for, that is finished.

clue.text: America embracing ally for NATO, perhaps

indicators.note: embracing says one piece wraps around another

parts.note: a crony is a close friend or ally

explanation.surface: The USA hugging a partner in the NATO alliance.
explanation.definitionFit: NATO is formed from the initials of North Atlantic Treaty Organization, an example of such a word.

clue.text: Fellow admitting compiler's lower in status

indicators.note: admitting means letting another piece inside

parts.note: a dean is a college fellow
the compiler refers to himself as me, compiler is

explanation.surface: A college fellow confessing the setter is beneath him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compiler's' is 'compiler is', the setter, giving ME.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean is to degrade or lower someone in status or dignity.

clue.text: Part of bottom and seat

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of one's bottom rests on a chair.
explanation.definitionFit: An ottoman is an upholstered seat or footstool without a back.

clue.text: Almost go out and demand tabloids?

parts.note: a guttering candle flickers and nearly goes out
to press is to insist or demand

explanation.surface: Popular papers that nearly vanish yet still insist?
explanation.definitionFit: The gutter press means sensational tabloid newspapers.
